PTR53-69.summary: Isabella tells Estrada that the King of France broke the peace in Naples without cause, has sent his power by sea and land to the frontiers of Roussillon and Fuenterrabía, and has opened war in Aragon, Guipúzcoa and Galicia; the King of England is bound by the treaties to help defend what is theirs, and Estrada is to ask for two thousand English foot with ships.
PTR53-69.en:
You already know how the King of France broke the war against us in Naples some days ago without our giving him any cause
for it; and that we made with him every justification [..] we could in the world to avoid the war, seeking all the means
that could [..] for it; and we never could [..] how much [..] we made, and [?demands] with much [..] [?being] [..] his [..]
and in our [..] Narbonne; and now, certainly not content with that, he has sent all his power by sea and by land to the
frontiers of our kingdoms, the greater part to that of Roussillon and the rest to the other frontier, of [Fuen]terrabía,
to make on us all the war he can in them, as he has already broken the war upon us through the kingdom of Aragon and
through the province of Guipúzcoa, as in the kingdom of Galicia, with a certain fleet at sea; now [..] upon [..] with his
